subject: Substance Abuse Prevention and Dog Park Proposal
overview: The School Committee approved the implementation of a Narcan protocol for school nurses and reviewed extensive data regarding local substance abuse and youth mental health. The body also approved a proposal to apply for a grant to construct a public dog park on school-adjacent land behind the McGlynn School.

items.title: Student Recognitions
items.summary: Superintendent Belson recognized Ian Adams as a National Merit Semifinalist alongside several other commended students.

items.title: Proposed Dog Park at McGlynn School
items.summary: The committee approved moving forward with a grant application to the Stanton Foundation for a dog park behind the McGlynn School near the river, following a technical presentation on site drainage, ADA compliance, and separate areas for large and small dogs.

items.title: School Narcan Protocol
items.summary: The committee approved a new protocol to train school nurses in the administration of Narcan to respond to potential opioid overdoses on school grounds.

items.title: Routine Business and Personnel
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from October 5, 2015, alongside routine bills, fund transfers, and payrolls.

items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions
items.summary: The body adopted several resolutions congratulating the Mayor on the Peace Garden dedication and the birth of a grandchild, and celebrating the retirement of member Robert Skerry.

items.title: Substance Abuse Prevention and Mental Health Update
items.summary: Officials presented a comprehensive report on local overdose data and student survey results showing a general decline in drug use but alarming rates of depression among high school females.

items.title: Donation Acceptance
items.summary: Approved a $1,500 gift from Media Technologies Corporation to the Gator Trade Alliance.

items.title: College Fair and Financial Aid Night
items.summary: The committee accepted a report detailing upcoming college fair events and a program to help students with disabilities transition to higher education.

items.title: Common Core and Curriculum Analysis
items.summary: Curriculum leaders provided an analysis of the Common Core's integration into Massachusetts frameworks, arguing the standards maintain academic rigor while improving critical thinking skills.

items.title: Professional Development Day Program
items.summary: The committee reviewed the agenda for the November 3 professional day, which includes training on the new 'School Brains' information system and behavioral safety management.

items.title: Quarterly Financial Report
items.summary: The Director of Finance reported the general fund is 26.65% expended and provided updates on the transition to VoIP telephones and a new online payment system for tuitions and fees.

items.title: Superintendent's Update on Legislative Issues
items.summary: Superintendent Belson discussed his recent testimony regarding charter school funding and reviewed Medford's MCAS performance relative to comparable urban districts.
